summary: Four cascades off a ~100 m escarpment on Dang's northern rim, locally claimed as Gujarat's tallest waterfall, and almost entirely unvisited.
description:
Chimer is the deep-cut that outgrows its obscurity the moment you see it: near Chimer village on Dang's northern rim toward Songadh, a monsoon stream throws itself off an escarpment locally measured at around 327 feet, roughly 100 metres, in four falls, two large and two small. That figure would make it Gujarat's tallest by a wide margin, but it remains an unofficial local claim; the state's official material gives Girmal that title, and nobody with a survey instrument appears to have settled the argument.

What is not in dispute is the setting: dense forest, farm paths for an approach, and a viewing experience that requires walking in from the road through fields with no tourist infrastructure of any kind. Sources even disagree on which district it belongs to, Dang and Tapi listings both claim it, which tells you exactly how far off the circuit it sits.

June to September is the season; the falls run strongest July–September and fade fast after. Go with a local contact, keep expectations rustic, and treat every published fact, including these, as pending ground-truth.
highlights: Claimed ~100 m drop, unofficially Gujarat's tallest
Genuinely undiscovered, no infrastructure at all

modes.road: Via the Dang–Tapi border roads toward Chimer village from the Songadh/Vyara side; ask locally. Signage is absent
modes.rail: Vyara station is the practical railhead

access.last_mile: Walk from the road through farm paths to the viewing area; distance varies with route
access.road_condition: Rural tar then village tracks; slow in monsoon

seasonality.notes: Strongest July–September; fades quickly once the rains stop.

experience.photography_notes: The full four-fall amphitheatre needs a wide lens from across the bowl; mist drifts far in peak flow.

amenities.food: None, provision at Songadh or Vyara
amenities.guides: A local contact from Chimer village is strongly advised

warnings: Unfenced escarpment edges: keep well back; the drop is serious
Farm paths turn to slick mud in rain
No facilities and no quick rescue, group visits only

tips: Pair with the Waghai belt or Padam Dungari on the drive back toward Surat
The district boundary is genuinely ambiguous here: expect Tapi signage
Take the height claim as folklore until someone measures it

faqs.q: Is Chimer really taller than Girmal?
faqs.a: Locally, yes, the ~327 ft figure circulates widely. Officially, no measurement exists and Gujarat Tourism's material calls Girmal the state's tallest. This dataset records both claims honestly.
